maya: Heads-up — TangoHealth onboarding traffic shows a spike in p99 token latency (~20% increase YoY vs last week). Noticed after yesterday's model rollout. Digging in but wanted to start a proactive ops thread.

devon: ugh. Got the traces? any correlation with sequence length or concurrency?

maya: quick snapshot: p50 stable, p95 up ~8%, p99 up ~20%. CPU/GPU IO looks fine. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 65% for some routes. Suspect prefix mismatch after prompts changed.

maya: snippets:```
2026-03-21T18:02:11Z INFO req_id=abc123 route=/chat model=redwood-open-13b seq_len=512 tokens=74 p99_ms=842 cache_hit=false
2026-03-21T18:02:40Z INFO req_id=abc456 route=/chat model=redwood-open-13b seq_len=128 tokens=34 p99_ms=190 cache_hit=true
```

olivia: thanks for the data. Renewal check: TangoHealth renewal in 42 days. This is a timely risk if UX degrades. Can we propose quick mitigations to lower latency and cost impact?

maya: my recommendation (proactive, low-risk):
- short-term: enable per-route prefix caching and force-readiness for the onboarding routes (toggle in Console).
- immediate pilot: run an int8 quantized variant for non-LLM-critical routes (canary 5% of traffic) to reduce GPU memory and bump throughput.
- if cache warmup doesn't recover p99, fallback to compact model (redwood-compact-8B) for heavy-tail queries routed by policy.

devon: agree. Also add a routing policy that pins high-frequency sessions to Dedicated pool during onboarding windows. That buys consistent latency.

raj: I'll loop in the account team. We should phrase this to Tango as "performance optimization pilot" — presentable outcomes: p99 reduction, cost delta, impact on quality metrics. Can we estimate quality delta for int8 vs baseline?

maya: quick A/B baseline we ran shows ROUGE-ish eval on our onboarding prompt set: int8 drop <0.7% BLEU-equivalent for the specific extraction tasks used by Tango. We'll include the eval deck.

maya: Proposed rollout plan:
1) Today: enable prefix cache & add a short TTL bump for onboarding routes. ops to watch.
2) 48h: enable int8 canary 5% traffic on sandbox, run eval deck + latency/cost dashboards.
3) 5–7 days: expand to 25% if quality/latency look good.
4) 10–14 days: if stable, add model-swap rule: route >1s p99 sessions to redwood-compact-8B with automatic fallthrough to baseline model if outputs fail checks.

ops-bot: ACTION CREATED: /runs/quant-canary-4288 — owner=devon, start=2026-03-22T10:00Z, canary=5%

devon: I'll own the canary. Quick ops checklist:
- create canary config:```json
{
  "route": "/onboard/*",
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "model_variant": "redwood-open-13b-int8",
  "fallback": "redwood-open-13b"
}
```
- enable dedicated pinning during 9am-6pm PST onboarding window
- monitor cache hit, p50/p95/p99, qual regression on prompt set

olivia: I'll prep the customer-facing note: short summary, risk mitigation, expected timeline, and a one-paragraph rollback plan. @raj can you handle contract/renewal framing?

raj: will do. Also request pricing impact estimate from pricing ops and add to the pilot doc.

maya: one more thing — capture feedback during the canary: ask Tango engineers 2 quick questions after a canary session: 1) any visible hallucination/regression? 2) any latency regressions on their side? We'll add to the post-canary survey.

devon: logging/alerts we'll wire: alert if p99 > baseline*1.15 for >5m OR cache_hit_rate < 60% for >10m.

maya: sounds good. Next steps: devon to spin canary config (ETA: 2 hours), ops-bot will mark run, olivia to draft customer note (ETA: EOD), raj to prep renewal note (ETA: tomorrow morning).

olivia: ping me when canary is active, I'll schedule a 30m sync with Tango engineers.

maya: thanks team :thumbsup: — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the run.

devon: started config now. will post status updates here.

ops-bot: STATUS: canary deploy started at 2026-03-22T10:03Z. monitors attached: latency-dashboard (onboard route), quality-eval-run-4288.
